permanentSolutions.description: One-time capital investments that create permanent infrastructure.

clean_water_infrastructure.beneficiaries: 2 billion people without safely managed drinking water
clean_water_infrastructure.quote: The average cost for World Vision to equip one person with access to clean water is $50. For 2 billion people: $100 billion

housing_infrastructure.description: Adequate housing for 1.6-3 billion people in inadequate housing/slums by 2030
housing_infrastructure.beneficiaries: 3 billion people (40% of world population) needing adequate housing by 2030
housing_infrastructure.quote: By 2030, 3 billion people (40% of world population) will need access to adequate housing, translating into 96,000 new affordable homes every day
housing_infrastructure.note: No consolidated global cost estimate available; need is massive and ongoing

electricity_universal_access.quote: Ensuring universal access to electricity by 2030 requires annual investment of $50 billion average

electricity_expansion.quote: Annual investment in electricity generation in developing countries needs more than double by 2035—from $280 billion today to $630 billion

perpetualPrograms.description: Annual recurring costs for humanitarian programs (2025-2026 figures).

tb_programs.beneficiaries: Global tuberculosis prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care
tb_programs.quote: US$22 billion required annually for TB prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care. In 2024, only US$5.9 billion was available (27% of target)

malaria_programs.quote: 2025 funding target: US$9.3 billion. 2024 funding was US$3.9 billion. Projected shortfall: US$5.4 billion

hiv_aids_programs.beneficiaries: Global HIV/AIDS prevention, treatment, and care (low/middle-income countries)
hiv_aids_programs.note_2026: UNAIDS reports needs up to $29.3B by 2025, but long-term target is $21.9B/year by 2030
hiv_aids_programs.quote: Estimated $21.9 billion needed annually by 2030 for AIDS response in low- and middle-income countries

food_security_wfp.note: WFP 2025 needed $16.9B but only received portion. 2026 target reduced to $13B to reach 110M
food_security_wfp.quote: WFP aims to reach 110 million of the most vulnerable at an estimated cost of $13 billion in 2026

food_security_full.note: Full cost to end hunger. WFP 2026 realistic funding is $13B, full need is ~$40B
food_security_full.quote: WFP needs approximately $40 billion per year to feed all of the world's hungry people

combined_three_diseases.description: TB ($22B) + Malaria ($9.3B) + HIV/AIDS ($21.9B) combined annual cost
combined_three_diseases.source: Compiled from WHO and UNAIDS 2025-2026 reports

perpetualFund.description: The power of investment returns: $50B annually without touching the principal.

returns_5_percent.description: $1 trillion invested at 5% annual return generates $50 billion per year forever
returns_5_percent.assumption: Conservative 5% annual return on $1 trillion principal (4% is very conservative, 6-7% is typical stock market)

covers_three_diseases_nearly_exactly.surplus: Covers 94% of all three major disease programs with annual returns alone
covers_three_diseases_nearly_exactly.interpretation: The growth of this single person's wealth annually nearly matches what the world needs to fund all three major disease programs forever

sourceNotes.dataYear: 2025-2026 data used where available; 2024 baseline adjusted for most recent figures
sourceNotes.gdpData: IMF World Economic Outlook 2026 forecasts in nominal USD
sourceNotes.healthData: WHO 2025 reports (TB, Malaria); UNAIDS 2025-2026 updates; WFP 2026 outlook
sourceNotes.wealthInequality: Oxfam and World Inequality Database current data
sourceNotes.methodology: All figures extracted from institutional reports. URLs point to primary/authoritative sources.
